output.brief: The rejects come from one specific combination: Arnholt resin dried in Press 5's dryer (D5), which has been degraded since late July. Arnholt arrives wetter, about 0.27–0.33% water at the dryer inlet against 0.12–0.14% for Quillan. D5 can't dry it below the 0.20% limit. Quillan through D5 is fine (0.9%). Arnholt through the healthy dryer on Press 7 is fine (0.8%). Arnholt through D5 runs about 10% rejects, on both shifts and for new and experienced operators alike. A same-lot test confirms it: dried in a good portable dryer it gave 0.8% rejects, and through D5 it gave 10.4%. So the new operators are not the cause, and dropping Arnholt is not needed. Do not put the six operators on improvement plans. This week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore its alarm limit to −40, and verify the dew point. Keep Arnholt off D5 until then, and check feed-throat moisture on every VX lot. Also check why Arnholt arrives wetter; north-annex storage is a plausible but unproven cause, because the samples can't separate storage from supplier. Don't pay for relocation yet. I'm fairly confident in the main finding.
